cands: Affirmative conclusion from a negative premise
Confusing an explanation with an excuse

items.text: Dogs are clearly better family pets, and everyone who’s ever lived with one knows it. So there’s really no reason to argue about it anymore.
A: No indoor basketball games are played in the rain. B: Some of our weekend games are indoor basketball games. A: So some of our weekend games are played in the rain.
gold: Affirmative conclusion from a negative premise

items.text: You shouldn’t hand cash to everyone who asks, because once you start doing that people will keep coming back. If someone says they need fifty bucks for rent, the safest rule is to never give out money to anyone who asks.
If he really got the speeding ticket, there’d be a court date on the notice. This notice has a court date, so he must have been caught speeding.

If the finance guy on TV says we should move our savings into bonds, why would I listen to him? He’s clearly clueless if he still dresses like that and talks like he owns the place. I’m keeping my money where it is.

“I think the new blood pressure meds might be making me dizzy.” If you were really sure, you wouldn’t be second-guessing it after one rough morning. You’re probably just anxious, not reacting to the pills.

The battery app says my phone lost only 4% overnight, so the battery is fine. If the app was off, then the charger must have been leaking tiny amounts of power all week, which would explain the random shutoffs.
If the movie was either badly written or just too long, I'm leaning badly written because the pacing kept dragging. So it wasn't really the length that hurt it.
The old courthouse should stay standing because it’s watched over this town for a century and clearly wants to keep doing its job.
I’m telling you, keep your savings in cash for now—people are saying the banks are getting shaky again, and I’m not risking my paycheck on a system everyone seems worried about.
I’m sick of this advice to just “watch what you eat”; I heard that cutting out gluten fixes most stomach problems, so I’m done wasting money on doctors.
I don't care that people are calling my balance patch 'bad'—I've shipped three top-selling games and they haven't. If I say the recoil is fine, that's probably because I know what works.
We should back the mayor's new transit plan because she's built a career winning elections and running campaigns, so her judgment on this is obviously better than the critics' whining.

A: "Nadia Vale just said everyone should binge that new mystery series, and she’s way more plugged in than we are." B: "Then I’m starting it tonight; if she thinks it’s worth watching, that settles it."
If Keon Mercer says our school should switch to four-day weeks, that’s good enough for me, because someone that successful understands what students need.

Stop pretending that the pastor’s story is genuine — he skipped the meal because he secretly knew the donated bread had been left in the fellowship hall by a kid in a blue hoodie at 2:17, and nobody else even saw that. People only make up details that specific when they’re trying to sound holy.

That actor didn't “improvise” the scene at all; he already knew the camera operator had been crying in the hallway after getting a call from her sister, so he timed his pause to look noble. Nobody guesses that much from a normal performance unless they know the whole private backstory.
If we want a serious budget plan, we need to align the CBO, GDP, CPI, FTE, and MOU targets before the caucus meets. Honestly, anyone who understands policy knows this is the only practical approach.

Everyone around here keeps saying cash is outdated, but if that many people still use debit and tap-to-pay, then cash has to be on its way out. You can see it at every store line, so there’s no point pretending bills still matter.

A: People are saying the new mayor’s tax plan is the only sensible one.
B: Then it probably is. If that many voters and local commentators are behind it, there must be something solid there.

I'm telling you, homework can't really be learning. I checked the dictionary, and it says learning is gaining knowledge or skill, not filling out worksheets after class. So when a teacher piles on pages of problems, that isn't learning, it's just busywork.

If the lab keeps losing samples, we need a fix today, not after another committee meeting. The quick answer is to skip the calibration step and just start the test, because at least then we're doing something.
If you're serious about dinner, you can order the burger or the chicken sandwich, but either one comes with the fries I’m charging extra for.

A: So are you joining the Saturday league or the Sunday one? Either way, I’ll put your name down and you can sort the rest later.
B: I haven’t said I’m joining anything.
A: It’s just a matter of which day works better.

After Maribel spent three weekends digging through train schedules, old blog posts, and connection maps to prove the overnight bus is the best way to get to Lisbon, I’m convinced it really is the best option.

A: "We should switch to later school start times because so many students are exhausted in first period."
B: "No way, if the district admitted that, parents would just keep pushing for more changes and the whole schedule would fall apart. So the current start time has to be fine."
If this game were really fair, I wouldn't keep losing ranked matches after work. The devs can't have made it balanced, because accepting that would mean all the hours I put in don't matter.
You said you "watch the baby in the bath," so you must be using your phone instead of actually paying attention. Please don’t leave him alone like that.
The chef told us the soup is light, so there’s barely any food in it and it’s not worth ordering. I’m skipping it.

Look, I’m just a regular guy juggling work, bills, and a bad back, and I know what actually helps: a daily multivitamin, a brisk walk, and eight hours of sleep. All that fancy detox tea stuff is for people with too much time. Most normal people can tell the simple stuff works, so you should stick with that too.

A: I think we should slow down and talk before moving in together.
B: I hear you, but I’m just saying what any normal person wants after a year together is to stop overthinking and make it official. I’m not some relationship expert, just someone who works, pays rent, and wants a real life with someone. So if you’re a normal person too, you’ll see that moving in is the sensible next step.
"Your numbers don't add up." They don't need to for someone with faith; you have to trust that this new pipeline plan is the right answer for the planet even if the spreadsheets look messy right now.
If you have faith in this company’s future, you’ll see that taking out this huge loan now is the smart move, even though the budget looks impossible on paper.
Our party should back the fresh slate of candidates with no baggage, because politics needs a modern reset and the old guard belongs to another era.

"Coach says we should keep playing him at shortstop, so why are you making a fuss?" I’m with Coach on this one, and if people on this team really back the club, they’ll trust his call instead of second-guessing it.

Most families still keep cash in a jar for emergencies, and honestly that's the sensible way to do it. If that's how most people handle money, it's the safer and better choice than all these weird app-only wallets.

We rolled out the new scheduling app and it cut missed shifts in half, but I still don't trust it. It just feels wrong to let a system decide who gets what shift, so I think we should go back to the old spreadsheet.

I know the paycheck app says the numbers are right, but this whole bonus structure feels off to me. If it feels that off, there has to be something shady going on, because I can usually tell when money doesn't add up.

“You missed three shifts in a row, so you’re being written up.” Come on, I’ve been sleeping on my sister’s couch and trying to juggle two bus rides just to get here. After everything I’m dealing with, you can’t seriously hit me with a write-up.

If you keep insisting that vaping is harmless, fine, but don’t act surprised when you’re coughing up blood at thirty. Doctors are always warning about lung damage for a reason. You either quit now or you’re gambling with a collapse that could leave you on oxygen for the rest of your life.

"Rent control will scare landlords away." That’s exactly why we can’t let it pass. If we keep pushing policies like that, building owners will stop maintaining units and the whole neighborhood will slide into unsafe, unlivable apartments.

I’m still not convinced by lab-made meat. If something grew in a tank instead of in the ground or in an animal, it just feels wrong to eat, and I’d rather stick with food that comes from real plants and livestock.

Old farming towns had hard lives, sure, but people were closer to the land and ate what nature gave them, not all these processed foods and chemicals. I’d take that way of life over modern convenience any day.

A: The apartment manager says there was "enough interest" in the unit to pick someone else, but I don’t care how they decided it. I just want this rental search to be over, so I’m going to assume they picked the most qualified person and move on.
Can’t believe the sprinkler stopped leaking right after the plumber tightened that fitting. Honestly, I think it was just lucky timing, not because he actually fixed anything.
I’m not stressing about the interview tomorrow. It’s possible they’ve already picked me because my last project was exactly what they needed, so I’m basically in.
You can’t say the budget airline will lose your bag on this trip. It’s possible it won’t, so I’m just going to assume everything will be fine and book it.

“This meal-prep thing is just rice, chicken, and vegetables, so it can’t really be that healthy.” If it were actually good for you, I’d be able to see why without needing a nutrition podcast and a spreadsheet.

A: I think the new patch made the game feel slower.
B: Come on, it’s common sense that balancing a game means making strong weapons weaker, so the patch was necessary.
If the class keeps turning in late homework, the answer is obvious: shorter deadlines and more reminders. It’s common sense that students do better when they feel a bit of pressure.

A rookie on a ranked squad and a guy who’s played this game for five years should be treated the same in matchmaking. If one of them gets a ban for quitting early, both should get the same penalty, because fairness means identical treatment.

You keep talking about the data, but have you thought about what it means for families when this test is delayed again? People are scared, waiting, and getting worse by the day, so clearly the agency needs to approve it right now.

I don’t care what the training manual says; if you’ve ever looked into a rescue dog’s eyes, you know the shelter should let people adopt the shy ones without so many forms. Those dogs are sitting in kennels longing for a home, and it’s heartbreaking.
"We should keep the old parking rules." Come on, you’re one of the smartest people in the council, so you can see that my plan to open the lots later is the obvious choice.

If we start letting people pick and choose every part of religion that feels convenient, next we’ll be in church on Sunday and bargaining with God like He’s a cable package. Faith isn’t a buffet where you grab the parts you like and leave the rest.

Marta from accounting told us the new salad bar is definitely the healthiest lunch option because she follows a lot of nutrition pages online. If she says the turkey wrap is the best choice, that's good enough for me.

We can't just ignore the river cleanup plan when Dr. Saito, who's a famous pediatrician, says the plastic ban is unnecessary. If a doctor thinks it's overblown, then the project probably isn't worth the cost.
Obviously cash is the best payment method. You can literally hold it in your hand, so it should be clear enough that it beats cards and apps.

“We should expand the bike lanes downtown.” No way—I hope the drivers who keep blocking the streets get stuck behind every red light for the next month, so I’m voting against it just to make their commute miserable.

Honestly, all the policy memos and expert panels are just people talking in circles. You don't need a degree to see the city council is wasting money, and anybody with common sense can tell this tax plan will just leave regular workers worse off.
Our striker is the best finish in the league, period. He’s the best finish in the league, and every stat I’ve seen backs that up because he’s the best finish in the league.

A: The school shouldn’t make us take phones away at the door.
B: Excuse me? After everything those kids pull in class, you’re still defending this? Any policy that gives them more chances to text, cheat, and disrespect teachers is obviously the right one.
“It’s just a tiny service charge, not a big deal.” No, it’s a rip-off, and I’m furious that restaurants keep sneaking this onto the bill, so clearly it’s unfair.

“You say screen time limits, but the real issue is I’ve been consistent about bedtime, meal routines, and keeping the tablet out of the bedroom. The only thing I’m still unsure about is whether two cartoons on rainy days is too much.”
“Then you clearly don’t have a real plan if you’re still unsure about cartoons.”

A: Did you use the last of the oat milk?
B: ...
A: Yeah, that’s what I thought. You finished it and didn’t want to admit it.

People keep trying to separate 'useful AI' from 'replacing people,' but there isn't some magic second where a helpful tool turns into a job-stealing machine. If the line is blurry, then the distinction doesn't really mean anything.
A newly discovered mineral in that cave could be harmless, but until any lab proves it doesn’t affect the lungs, we should assume it’s dangerous and ban the whole site.
I haven’t seen any report proving that the river cleanup plan will hurt the wetland, so I’m telling everyone to support it and stop doubting it.
One guide says Barcelona is the best city break in Europe and another says it’s overrated; the sensible view is that it’s probably just average, somewhere in the middle.

If Liora, who owns three businesses and never has to worry about a paycheck, says the downtown tax hike will hurt small employers, I’m inclined to believe her over the city planner with a modest salary.
Saw your text about the parking ticket appeal. Since you said the officer is corrupt, your whole case is trash and you should just pay it.
A: You said the airport shuttle is late because the driver is tired. B: That reasoning is sloppy, so the shuttle probably isn't actually late.

A: The lab report says the hit-and-run description matches only one in a few hundred drivers in this city.
B: Still, he's the guy who lives closest to the scene and he looked nervous in court. That kind of thing doesn't happen by chance, so I think the statistics are missing the real picture.
People keep saying the city should not fund the new statue because the bridge repairs are overdue, but our town was built on faith, and that deserves to be seen downtown.
"Rent is up again and my landlord still hasn't fixed the heater." Well, the neighborhood is changing fast, and the coffee shop on the corner has great pastries now.
My cousin’s landlord says the new lease fee is legal, so it must be fine. I’m just paying it and not arguing with him.
"Most people can't handle saving money." Just look at the folks who borrow from payday apps and max out credit cards; if that's the crowd we're seeing, then adults are basically terrible with money.
Every time I open the app store, the top reviews are from people with glitches and crashes. Honestly, that proves most new phones are a mess.
The city budget got tight because they keep wasting money on consultants. If they’d stop hiring outside firms for everything, the budget problem would be gone.

The audit keeps getting delayed because three council members and the contractor keep swapping versions of the invoices. Every time someone asks for the originals, a file is “misplaced” or suddenly redacted. That’s exactly why the bribery story is real: they’re hiding the proof.
The fire at the city theater is a setback, sure, but now the council will have to pour money into rebuilding downtown, hire crews, and finally give the whole district the attention it’s been needing.
The arena roof collapsed, but honestly that means a ton of contractors, suppliers, and promoters get work, so the whole music scene around here is probably better off now.

The trip looks great from the reviews I checked: the hotel has photos of the ocean view, one blog said the train ride was easy, and a couple people mentioned the old town was beautiful. I’m booking it tonight and not worrying about the rest.
You only think that meal kit is worth it because you love anything with a fancy label. So your opinion on it is basically biased, and the sauce probably isn’t even that good.

"The new show is getting rushed reviews because the finale actually works." Sure, but you’re the kind of coworker who always sides with the big franchise, so of course you’re saying that. Your take doesn’t count.

School is where you learn things, because if you’re learning, that’s what makes it school. That’s why missing class matters so much, since the whole point of school is to be the place where learning happens.
"This neighborhood is affordable." That just means people can afford it, which is why it’s affordable in the first place.
A: Why do you call that result reliable? B: Because it’s a trustworthy result. If the measurements weren’t trustworthy, I wouldn’t call them reliable.
If a laptop has a solid-state drive, it boots up fast, so whenever you see one booting up fast, you can tell it has a solid-state drive.
“I still haven’t been paid for last Friday’s shift.” Then why did you spend the paycheck before asking for more hours?
The lab report says this new battery lasts forever and needs a weekly recharge, so it’s basically the perfect upgrade.

Our manager keeps pushing that new performance app because he gets a bonus when the department “adopts” it. So no, I’m not taking his praise of it seriously; if his paycheck depends on us buying in, his recommendation is basically worthless.

A: Dr. Sethi says I should get the booster.
B: Of course she does—she runs a clinic and gets paid when people come in. Her advice is obviously just about keeping the appointments coming, not about what’s best for patients.

A: The train line got delayed again, and nobody can tell me why the signal keeps dropping in that one tunnel.
B: Exactly, after all these years, if they still can't explain it, they probably never will. We should just assume that stretch of track is impossible to fix.

I’m tired of people acting like the studio was wrong for canceling the show. The ratings dipped after the cast change, the ad buyers pulled back, and the network needed something cheaper to fill the slot. That’s why they dropped it, and honestly that makes sense.
gold: Confusing an explanation with an excuse

items.text: "He texts every morning and remembers the little things, so he's a better match than someone who only texts every morning." But the second part is what makes the first one matter, so the more detailed version is more likely to be the real sign of a good relationship.
Ever since we got a second cat, the apartment feels calmer and everyone’s sleeping better. Honestly, cats must be what’s making the whole household less stressed.
My cat can’t be both indoors and on the porch right now. She’s not indoors, so she must be out there by the back steps again.
If the bookstore had gotten enough customers on Saturday, they would have stayed open late. They closed at six, so they must not have done well that day.
You can’t call it a “disorder” when the word literally comes from “out of order,” so treating ADHD like a medical condition misses what it really means.

I’m pretty sure the landlord either raised the rent without notice or tried to charge everyone an extra fee, but the rent increase by itself is way more likely. Those big bad things almost never both happen in the same month.

If my son skips dinner tonight, he’ll probably ask for dessert or wake up hungry, but honestly the dessert request is more likely than either of those happening. Kids usually just want the sweet stuff.

A lot of people from that coastal town work in fishing or seasonal jobs, so I’m sure Lila is probably bad with money too. She grew up there, so she must be one of those people who never saves anything.

Lina: "You can't say a shelter cat and a rescue cat are the same thing." They aren't the same because this one was from the city shelter and that one was rescued by a volunteer, so the label matters. Either way, both came into the house with no owner, no history in my place, and I adopted them after they were taken in.

I don't mind when our studio adds product placement to a show because that's just how streaming pays for ambitious episodes, but if that other network stuffs ads into its drama, that's cheap and ruins the art.
I can forgive our candidate for missing the climate vote because the schedule was packed, but if the other side's senator skips one meeting for the same reason, that's lazy and unfit for office.

A: “The school is closed today.”
B: “Then there’s no school work to do, so we don’t need to study for the exam.”

If you’re in a committed relationship, you should be more committed than everyone else, so if my partner is “in a committed relationship,” that means they have to care more than any other person does.

A: All countries with a stable constitution protect free speech. All places that protect free speech allow peaceful protests. So some countries with a stable constitution allow peaceful protests.
B: That sounds right to me.
No fake reviews are honest. Some honest reviews are not useful. So some useful reviews are not fake reviews.
“We need to cut down on wasted hours.” No wasted hours are productive work. Some productive work is not overtime. So some overtime is not wasted hours.

A: What do you mean by "budget travel"?
B: It means moving through transit options in a deliberately low-cost mode, where the trip is structured around the least expensive pathways available.
"The inspection report says the bridge bolts are corroded, and the city logged three closures last winter. So if you still say the repairs can wait, you're just denying the facts."
Our city has one of the healthiest public gym programs in the state, so this neighborhood clinic should be perfectly healthy too.

If a relationship is like a team and a good team has clear roles, then letting one partner make all the decisions is basically the same as a coach calling every play, so that setup works fine for love too.

“My rabbit is calm when I sit near her, so she probably needs me around all the time.” That’s like how a toddler gets upset when a parent leaves, and since both need reassurance, I guess rabbits are basically tiny children.
Every app these days has some kind of privacy setting hidden in three menus, so some privacy setting is hidden in every app. That’s why I don’t trust this whole software scene.
If every student in this class can pass the quiz, then this class is obviously a strong class. That’s what matters when people talk about our school.
“Either we adopt a cat or we stay pet-free.” I don’t buy that—some people just foster for a while, and that works better anyway.

If the team is either good enough to win the league or it isn’t, then why are we pretending the issue is only the coach? The real answer is that the league schedule is brutal, and that’s what’s keeping us down.
If the other team is pushing this patch so hard, I’m not buying it. They’ve spent the whole season trashing our clan, so their take on balance changes is probably just bad by default.
They keep pushing this new factory because it will create jobs, but if the result is more people working, then the project is fine and everyone should stop complaining.

People act like switching from paper books to e-readers is a huge cultural loss, but we already moved from scrolls to codexes and from vinyl to streaming. It’s the same thing: a new format replaces an old one, and that’s just how history works.

“That new dress code rule is overkill.” Sure, and people laughed at the guy who said the Earth moved around the sun, too. When an idea gets mocked this hard, it usually means folks are just not ready for it yet, so I’m taking the rule seriously.
My ex says, "her cousin's therapist told her couples who argue over text are doomed," so there’s no point trying anymore. If a therapist said that, then the relationship is basically already over.

Our cat started sleeping by the crib right after the nursery was painted, and one local pet blog called that a sign pets can sense bad energy, so the whole house is probably warning us. That blog has done the research, so I’m not ignoring it.
I’m not taking the 6 a.m. train just to save twenty dollars. Either I fly and get there rested, or I drag myself through a miserable day in transit—those are the only sane options.
If the client wants the deck by Friday, then we either stay late tonight or miss the deadline. There isn’t some magic middle option where the work just finishes itself.
I’m telling you, my manager didn’t “misplace” my overtime sheet. Someone in payroll probably had a vendetta and erased it so I’d stop asking for a raise.
"It’s probably just a stomach bug." No, the clinic sent me home too fast because they didn’t want the numbers to look bad, and that’s why my fever kept climbing.
I know the coin has landed on heads five times, but that just means tails is due next. If we keep calling heads, we're probably just chasing the streak and setting ourselves up to lose again.

Why are people acting like a 6 a.m. flight is no big deal? If I can get up for work at 7, I can get up for a trip at 6. It’s the same thing: an alarm is an alarm, and adults should be able to manage it.
I’m not taking adoption advice from that rescue group. They partnered with the same shelter that had those neglect charges last year, so whatever they recommend is probably just as sloppy.

Our school is actually doing great academically. If you look at the last few years, the main classes have improved, and the students who apply themselves are fine. So yeah, the school is clearly successful.

Lina: Saying the landlord should have sold the place last year is easy now that rents jumped and the building got inspected. Back then, nobody had those numbers, so calling her stupid for holding onto it makes no sense.
Marek: The market looked normal then, but after everything changed, she had to have seen it coming.
The air has felt heavy and nasty all week, so this neighborhood’s pollution is clearly out of control and people need to admit it. I can smell it every time I step outside, and that should be enough.

A: I had two terrible managers in a row at that warehouse, so honestly most supervisors just micromanage and make work miserable.
B: That seems like a big leap.
A: Not really. If that many of them are like that in my experience, it’s probably how the whole thing works.
Just played three matches with randoms and every single one bailed as soon as we started losing. I’m done trying to team up with people online because random players are always selfish.

A: My dad keeps saying we should let kids figure things out on their own, but that advice comes from someone who was raised back in the 70s, so I don't buy it. B: Why not? A: Because if it comes from that old style of parenting, it's probably outdated and wrong for today.

These patch notes saying the new weapon is balanced are coming from a streamer who got sponsored by the studio, so they're obviously just propaganda. If the people paid by the game say it's fine, then it's not trustworthy.

A: How do you keep track of your spending so well? B: I just have this inner accountant who watches every purchase and tells me whether it fits the budget. That accountant probably has to keep notes too, otherwise how would it know what I can afford?
I’ve hit three scratch-off wins this week, so I’m definitely on a streak. I’m putting the extra money back into tickets tonight because this kind of run usually keeps going for a while.

"I just think toddlers need clear rules." Sure, kids do better with routine, boundaries help them feel safe, and consistency makes mornings easier. A calm house is a healthy house, so my strict bedtime plan is obviously the right way to raise children.
If the council had passed that housing plan last year, rent would be down by now and people wouldn’t be moving out of the city. They dragged their feet, so this mess is on them.

A: "If we had funded the new telescope, we'd already have found life on that moon."
B: "Exactly. Skipping that project cost us the biggest discovery in decades."

Speeding tickets are fines, and DUI charges are fines too, so speeding and drunk driving must be the same kind of offense. The city should treat them identically and stop acting like one is worse than the other.
All the places with good food near the station are crowded, and all the places with good coffee near the station are crowded. So the food spots and the coffee shops are really the same places.

"You keep calling the new meal plan 'cheap.' If you mean it in the good sense, it’s smart, filling, and finally stops the cafeteria from wasting money on overpriced bowls of mush. If you mean it in the bad sense, then it’s still a sensible change because people are tired of tiny portions dressed up like gourmet food."

A: "Is the new homework policy easier?" B: "If by easier you mean less busywork, yes, because students can actually learn without drowning in worksheets. If by easier you mean softer standards, then no, and that’s a good thing because school should stop lowering the bar every time parents complain."

People keep posting those videos of pit bulls snapping at neighbors, but I don’t buy that they’re really dog owners at all; those are probably cat people pretending to “rescue” dogs just so they can make dog owners look reckless.

A: That new tax plan is better.
B: Better than the last one? Better than the bill it replaced? Either way, people are going to feel it more in their paycheck and less in services.
All engineers know how to read a wiring diagram. No interns are engineers. So no interns know how to read a wiring diagram.
All good parents keep their kids safe. No parents who skip bedtime are good parents. So no parents who skip bedtime keep their kids safe.

I can't do this relationship thing anymore because I need total honesty, but I also never want to hear anything that might upset me. If you care about us, you should tell me everything and keep all the peace at the same time.

The nutritionist says butter is fine in moderation, the cardiologist says to avoid it, and the articles just keep arguing. Honestly, if the experts can’t even agree on butter, I’m not trusting any of them about what to eat.
We found a few dead fish near the river this morning, so the factory upstream must be dumping poison into the water. I’m posting this before the company has a chance to spin it.
I’m keeping my son off those allergy meds. The doctor can print all the pamphlets he wants, but I know what’s best for this family, so that’s the end of it.
The lab finally got the samples back in under an hour, so the new centrifuge must be what fixed our turnaround. No need to keep blaming staffing or the broken label printer.

A: I’ve been having these headaches all week.
B: It’s just the new glasses. Once you wear them a bit, the headaches will stop.
No cats are dogs, so any non-dogs must be non-cats.
Some basketball players are left-handed, so some non-left-handed people are non-basketball players.
I'm not booking the overnight bus to Porto. If the driver gets tired, one mistake on a dark road and we're all done for. I'll pay more for a daytime train and know I'll get there alive.

A: I'm skipping the sushi place and just getting fries. What if the fish has been sitting out and I spend the whole night sick?
B: The odds are probably fine, but I don't want to gamble with my stomach today. Fries are at least something I know won't wreck me.
We got to Lisbon and the whole place just feels organized and calm. That’s because it’s a European city, so of course it works better than most places.

B: “That rifle in the game is overpowered.” A: Every weapon people complain about is a weapon with high damage, and every weapon with high damage is an overpowered weapon, so every overpowered weapon is one people complain about.

Kestrel’s theory about the old factory district just says the area changed because the mills closed and people moved out. That may fit this one neighborhood, but it doesn’t explain the bigger shifts in the city or any other period of decline. So it’s more of a label for that one episode than a real historical explanation.
That diner isn't serving food, it's unloading greasy junk onto plates. Nobody should have to pay for that sloppy, unhealthy mess, so the place is obviously trash.

Yeah, I get that the new recycling rule is meant to keep more trash out of the landfill, but you said it would work "for most households," and I need you to be exact about what counts as most. Is that 51 percent, 67, or 89? Until you give me a number I like, the whole thing is too vague to take seriously.

"I’m keeping some cash in my savings account because markets can turn fast." That sounds cautious, but the long-run average return on stocks is higher, so the rational move is to put nearly everything into index funds and stop worrying about emergency savings.

"This phone update broke your battery?" Sure, maybe, but the bigger problem is that the update barely changed anything useful. And if you’re saying it changed too much, that’s exactly why I won’t install it.

“The coach says our defense looks lost.” I don’t care what it looks like if the numbers are good: we’re holding teams to 88 points a game and the turnover count is down. That’s the only thing that matters, so the defense is clearly fine.
